A Talk Cum Demo on understanding Publication reach out – Visibility and Citation impact was organized by the Central Library on 17 th November, 2018 at 11:30AM in the College auditorium as part of the National Library Week celebration.

Dr. Sunil M.V Librarian, SDMIMD, Mysore was the resource person of the day. Mr. Ronald Prakash Cutinha, Librarian & IQAC Coordinator of the college briefly introduced the resource person and welcomed. Agenda of the talk was to focus on:

Understanding Publication Reach-out Impact Factor – for journal purpose h-Index- for individuals Research Networking Tools How to create Google Scholar Account, ORCID and Research Gate Account? He highlighted the importance of profile creation of the faculty in the areas of their expertise and how Research Networking tools help to organize, discover, disseminate, making visible the research and scholarly information. He explained about Core Strength of RN Tools and what are the benefits of these RN tools and which all the tools that are best in market to use to get better impact factor and H- index number. He also inspired the entire faculty to take up research activities and publish more and more papers in UGC peer reviewed journals or Thomson ISI listed journals.

Dr. Sunil also mentioned about various RN tools like iamreseracher, ResearcherID, ReserchGate, Academia, Linkedin and Mendely across pure sciences, humanities/social sciences, Art & literature domains.

The session got continued with demo on how to open an account in Google Scholar and how Google Citation services help any author in tracking his/her own publication. Dr. Sunil showed couple of demonstrative videos on how to create a profile in Google Scholar.One of the PG faculty Dr. Noor Mubasheer of the Social Work department opened her account on Google Scholar and experienced on Google Citation Services.

Dr .Sunil concluded his talk by motivating teachers to market their credentials and on how Research Network will benefit your parent organization and thereby benefiting the country’s’ academic output.

The entire illustrative session was more interactive and informative. Final few minutes were kept aside for discussion and the faculty clarified their doubts related to research, publication and topic related to the talk.

The MOU was also intended to recognize the general basis for a collaborative working relationship between the two institutions in education, training and technical cooperation in chemistry related topics. They have agreed to jointly undertake internship programmes for chemistry students, faculty development programmes for the faculty of chemistry, project works, in-plant training, academic curriculum development and referral of chemistry students to pursue higher education plastic processing and moulding technology.

(R.T.Nagaralli, Director and Head, CIPE T -CSTS,Mysuru and Dr.T.Ruth Shantha Kumari, Principal, St.Philomena’s College(Autonomous), Mysuru are seen exchanging the signed MOU. Rev.Dr.Bernard Prakash Barnis, Rector/Manager and Rev.Fr.Maria Xavier, Vice-Rector of the college are also seen)

The MOU was executed during a signing ceremony held at the conference hall of St.Philomena’s College in the presence of teaching staff of the college. The said MOU was signed by R.T.Nagaralli, Director and Head and Suman,the Administrative Officer, both for CIPET-CSTS side whereas for St.Philomena’s College, the signatories were Dr.T.Ruth Shantha Kumari, the Principal of the college and Rev.Dr.Bernard Prakash Barnis, the Rector/Manager of the institution.

During the occasion, Principal, Dr.Ruth Shantha Kumari said that signing of the MOU is a defining moment for both the institutes and such partnership will facilitate the institutes in achieving larger goals of self-reliance. She also called upon the staff of the college to be motivated from this and put efforts to enter into agreements with other reputed institutions.

R.T.Nagaralli, the Director/Head of CIPET-CSTS gave a brief introduction of CIPET-CSTS institute through power point presentation. He urged the staff to motivate the students to take up skilled training in the form of internship, project work etc.
Dr.RaviJ.D.Saldanha, Associate Professor in Chemistry, St.Philomena’s College(Autonomous), Mysuru welcomed. Mr.Ronald Prakash Cutinha, IQAC co-ordinator of the college proposed a vote of thanks.

title: IV CONVOCATION CEREMONY OF ST. PHILO’S
summary: St. Philomena’s college organised its 4 th convocation ceremony on September 28, 2018 at college indoor stadium. A total of 7 Under-Graduate and 8 Post-Graduate students were honoured with stream-wise Gold Medals and 29 Under-Graduates with gold Medals based on their subjects.
content: St. Philomena’s college organised its 4 th convocation ceremony on September 28, 2018 at college indoor stadium. A total of 7 Under-Graduate and 8 Post-Graduate students were honoured with stream-wise Gold Medals and 29 Under-Graduates with gold Medals based on their subjects.

The chief Guest, Justice V. Gopala Gowda, Retd. Judge of Supreme Court of India addressed the gathering told that, “Education is a special manifestation of man; education is a treasure that can be preserved without the fear of loss”, referring to a statement evolved during the case of Unnikrishnan A. P. in the SC. Destiny of nation is shaped in a classroom were a teacher is the sculptor who sculpts multi talented students and inspire them to show interest in various subject. He also added the importance of quality of education as it is the solution to all problems.

His Excellency Most Rev. Dr. K. A. William, Bishop of Mysore spoke in his presidential remarks that, “The best convocation is the satisfaction of being a good human being”. He emphasized on the prominence of education and spreading of same to all directions. Always do good; think good and speak good and thus become useful to the society he added. Universities or colleges are not mere workshops which manufacture trivial degree holders but they should produce personalities with good values.

The guest of Honour, Prof. Aisha M. Sheriff, Vice Chancellor of Mysore University told in her speech that St. Philomena’s College, established in late 1946, has a Royal Legacy as it has honour and privilege of being declared open by His Highness, Sri. JayachamarajendraWodeyar, late Maharaja of Mysore. She also mentioned recent milestones of the college including its achievement as the first degree college in Karnataka state to be accredited with A+ grade by NACC. She remarked the college as a global village with students from 19 different states of the country and 26 foreign countries.Addressing the graduates gathered she asked them to“Dream and Dream Big”. Never seize learning and treat humanity as a religion she added.

A total of 255 UG and 132 PG students were awarded with the certificates. Msgr. Rev. Leslie Moras Vicar of Educational Institutions and Health Care management (MDES), Rev. Fr. Vijay Kumar, Secretary of MDES, Rev. Dr. Bernard Prakash Barnis, Rector and Manager of the College, Dr. Ruth Shanthakumari, Principal, Orthbert Pinto, Director of PG and Dr. Alphonsus D’Souza, Controller of Examinations were present on the dais.

title: Field Visit To JanaDwani Community Radio – Sarguru
summary: Organized for: 5th Semester B.voc Students (Media and Entertainment)
content: Organized for: 5th Semester B.voc Students (Media and Entertainment)
Date: 30TH AUGUST 2018
Agenda: To Make Students Aware Of working of Community Radio, its functions, the radio setup and Its purpose in the society.
Number of Students : 18
Outcome of the Visit: Better understanding of the way the small community radio station operates, a first-hand experience.

Through the visit the students first interacted with the Coordinator of the Radio Station Mr. Shiva Kumar, who explained the working of the set up and briefed them the programmes carried on. He also spoke about the history of the community radios and its purpose and role in development. Students were made aware of the programmes and policies that the government from both centre and state under take to promote this initiative and what are the policies with regards to the same.

While talking on various community radio aspects, it was made to understand that how important it is to access the quality information and to mainstream the local communities for holistic development. This also includes the talk on Article 19 (1)(a), the root for community radio movement.

The interaction session was followed by Q & A sessions where, students were spirited to ask and know more about the community issues handled, the redressal if any in socio –political arena that is seen after voicing same in the radio, the participation from local community, the working cost of the set up and many such related topics and issues.

This was followed by, visit to control room, where the production, input, output process is done. The Coordinator explained the working and use of software and amplifiers for broadcasting and such other aspects of networking. The students were fortunate enough to see a live recording of a interview with local artist which helped them to understand the lucidity in the interview, the language used and how it is different when compared to public and commercial broadcasts.

title: Independence Day 2018
content: INDEPENDENCE DAY CELEBRATION
Tri colour flutters high at St. Philomena's College
On the occasion of the 72nd Independence Day St. Philomena’s College paid a tribute to the nation by hoisting the national flag followed by a short program on August 15 in the college auditorium.

" Mrs. Madhuri Tatachari, Managing trustee of Bhramara Trust, was the Chief Guest. Addressing the students she explained what Independence really means. Independent is to have complete growth where every person in that area has no fear to express his feelings. Everyone has the right to live differently. Liberty of one individual should not hurt the liberty of another. People may aspire to have freedom, but it should be freedom from selfishness, anger, malice, hatred etc. We should be masters of ourselves. According to dictionaries Independence is the complete control of a group of people over a particular area but that is where the contradiction lies. Complete control and then call it Independence? She briefed on how Independence, freedom and liberty are closely connected and yet not the same. Total Independence is something impossible to achieve but peaceful I nter-Dependence is the key. No human being can say ‘I am all alone’. She quoted Thomas Merton’s book ‘No man is an island’. We live in society not in isolation. A good friend is the one who corrects you by hitting on your head. We cannot change the world, better we change ourselves.

Mrs. Madhuri Tatachari also shared her own experiences and how her mother taught her to respect all religions and about true love.She concluded by saying that a country where all the people are united and stay happy that is a truly free and Independent nation. Earlier National flag was hoisted by Rev. Fr. M. Vincent, Principal of St. Philomena’s PU College. The Chief Guest planted a sapling. ­­
‘Philoline’ a news letter by the Dept. of Journalism was released by Prof. Rajalakshmi, Dean of Science.
This was followed by patriotic songs and dances performed by the students. All teaching, non-teaching staff of the college and the students were present.

title: Orientation Program for First year students
summary: Orientation Program for First year students
content: Orientation Program for First year students
Internal Quality Assurance Cell (IQAC)
St.Philomena’s college (Autonomous)
Orientation Program For First year UG students
St Philomena’s college had organized an orientation program for the I degree (UG) students, in the indoor stadium for two days from July 20- 21,2018.

The stage saw the presence of dignitaries viz. Rev. Dr. Bernard Prakash Barnis, rector/ Manager , Rev Fr Maria Sunil Xavier, vice – rector , Dr. Ruth Shantha Kumari, Principal, Dr. Alphonsus D’souza, controller of examinations, Prof. Othbert Pinto, Director, P.G block, Rev. Fr. Rony Ravi Kumar, Asst Director, P.G block, MR. Ronald Prakash Cutinha, IQAC coordinator and Rev Fr Anthony Raj, warden of the Boys’ hostel.
The session began with prayer service and lighting of the lamp by students and the dignitaries present.
Session:1 Motivational Talk
In the first session Prof. Jose V.K, Former Principal, Teresian college, Mysuru spoke about ‘ Determinism and possibilism’ . He started the session with a quote which read,
“ Education does not mean teaching people what they do not know.
It means teaching them to behave as they do not behave .” – John Ruskin

He said that we live in ‘knowledge work world’, where knowledge is very important to make you effective. We must integrate whatever we learn into our life. He said that- to know and not to do, is really not to know, to learn and not to do, is really not to learn and to understand and not doing it, is really not understood .

He also said that there are two roads in life. They are the road of ‘Greatness ‘ the road less travelled and that of ‘mediocrity’ travelled by many. It is left to us to select the road we travel in our life.

Continuing his talk on motivation , he said ‘Survival is the first motivation to live’, where as love motivates relationship , learning motivates gowth and development and leaving a legacy motivates contributions to life. He conveyed the message that everyone should understand ‘ Life is short’ and ‘Nothing is imposible’.
He concluded the session with a quote which said ,
“ Few of us can do great things,
But all of us can do small things with great love” – Mother Teresa.
Session 2: Communication Skills

In the second session Prof.A.John Siluvai, HOD, P G dept of English, St.Philomena’s college Mysuru, spoke about ‘The necessity of proper communication skills’. He conveyed the message in a lively and humorous way.

During his talk he differentiated the body language of people which differs from country to country very humorously. He spoke about non-verbal communication which includes pitch, speed, tone, and volume of voice, gestures and facial expressions, eye movements and appearance. Regarding verbal communication, use of words to express yourself, he gave an example saying “NO” in various facial expressions and gestures comically. Following that he engaged an interaction session with students on correction of sentences, in which students actively participated.
Session 3: About the College

Dr.Alphonsus Dsouza, controller of examinations , gave the students a clear understanding of the present examination pattern of the college. He spoke about the choice based credit system (CBCS) which is extended for the (UG) courses. He explained semesterwise scheme of examination for all the streams, & The UGC recommended 10-point grading system. As per the university guidelines and also court directives, students who do not attend 75% of the total classes held, cannot appear for the end semester exams he said. He cautioned the students that there shall be no provision for improvement of IA marks scored once
Mr. Ronald Prakash Cutinna, the librarian and IQAC coordinator spoke about the various facilities available in the college and advised them to make the best use.

Prof.Anand, HOD, Dept. of Political science, motivated the students to take part in various extra-curricular activities conducted by the cultural committee throughout the year. He conducted a small activity to make students realize ‘we are good imitators; but we are not good initiators’, and motivated them to participate in all events.
Session: 4 Information Sources- Print and Online

The session was handled by Dr.C.P. Ramasesh, Retd. Librarian, University of Mysuru. During his talk he gave the complete details of the information sources available for students both in print and online.

He explained various types of books available for reference to studentsand taught the students ‘How to read a book’. Moving on to online sources he explained about number of websites specially meant for students’ guidance. DOAJ- Directory of Open Access Journals, gives 11000 e-journals for students and Amazon gives 50% offer on their books he specified. In the following session of the day, career guidance seminar was arranged for all the three streams.

Prof. Cletus D’souza, Retd. Professor, Dept of Biochemistry, University of Mysuru spoke about the importance of making a right choice as to which way to go after completing the course through a series of meaningfully chosen comic slides. He said to find a job of your interest, not a job which pays you high salary but you are not interested. Primary goal of life must be ‘Happiness’ not ‘Money’, he specified.

Money is not equal to success, when you are successful money automatically comes to you. Hence exploring your interests is the best way to choose a perfect job. He spoke about ‘Aptitude’ and ‘Attitude’- the two little things that make a big difference.

Your career planning should be started now! Don’t postpone the decision, he stressed. He also gave a caution saying-many of the jobs that are today will not be after ten years, there will be new things/jobs in this digital world, which no college teaches you but its of your own interest of exploring things and finding a job of your interest. He emphasized that there is ‘No short cut to success’and urged the students to realize the significance of hard work.He also gave a ‘pencil parable’ example which was applied to a student life and said Excel in whatever career you choose.

The session was handled by Dr. Parashiva Murthy, National level trainer and facilitator, Govt. First Grade college, T. Narasipura. He said 92% of engineers are unemployed. Life is not easy after 5 years, he cautioned the students and added that every week 5 students aged above 25, come to him, unemployed and depressed. He motivated the students to take risk in life and to be self confident. Dr. Parashiva Murthy urged the students to ensure that their stay in St.Philomena’s will be a turning point in life. He also quoted that ‘You are worth more than diamonds, have dreams in your life, remember first impression is the best impression, but the last is the everlasting one .
The session was headed by Dr.Prithvi Datta, faculty of KSOU, Mysore, a man of letters, an academic giant and an intellect.
Prof.Prithvi Datta started his talk by congratulating all the students for furnishing their schooling and entering into the portals of a degree college where next three years are got to be exciting.

He stressed on three things. First, the timeor era in which we live, second, what shoud be the education for students ,what are the strengths and limitations of learning that we are getting inside the classroom over the next three years and thirdly a little bit about what are the other kinds of prospects that exist. He also spoke about human species, DNA and increasing rate of life span. He sressed about the ways in which subjects like Political Science and Public Administration help us!

After streamwise interaction, all the students assembled in the indoor stadium for a concluding session. Some of the students gave suggestions and a feedback about the whole programme. Dr.Ruth Shantha Kumari proposed the vote of thanks. Rev.Dr.Bernard Prakash Barnis, Rector/Manager; Rev.Fr.Maria Sunil Xavier, Vice Rector; Dr.Ruth Shantha Kumari Principal, Prof.Sanjay Nair, Vice Principal; Dr.Alphonsus D’souza, Controller of Examinations; Prof.Othbert Pinto, Director, PG block; Rev.Fr.Rony Ravikumar, Asst Director, PG block; Mr.Ronald Prakash Cutinha, IQAC co- ordinator; Deans of Science, Commerce, Arts and languages; Prof.Anand ,HOD of Political Science; all the members of faculty and first year UG students were present in the orientation programme.

title: International Yoga Day
content: International Yoga Day

Yoga transcends all religions into one, makes mind and body flexible and the internal vision of the body is called Yoga, said Dr.A.R.Seetharam, Expert in yoga and value education and Principal, Sri Sharada college, Tamil Naidu, on 4 th International yoga day organized by St.Philomena’s college, Mysore on June 21, 2018 from 2 to 4:30 pm at the college indoor stadium.

Yoga also gives us the power of positive thinking, hope and courage to do the work which we thought we could never do it. While practicing yoga if you tell yourself ;I and body are different, I am not the thought, I am accepting anything that happens in my life and I never expect anything; you can see the changes in your behavior and also in your body, he said.

Yoga helps to manage stress which we cannot prevent and should also not do so; we should always take stress as our motivation to do any work given to us. Yoga also helps us to learn the art of living in present , active acceptance and not expecting anything ,he added.

Practically several asanas were demonstrated by Dr.Seethram and his team and they also taught a few easy asanas which can be practiced in our day to day life to the members of faculty and students of the college.

Rev.Dr.Bernard Prakash Barnis, Rector; Dr.Ruth Shantha Kumari, Principal; Rev.Fr. Maria Xavier, Vice Rector; Prof.V.Sanjay Nair, Vice principal; Rev.Fr.Rony Ravi Kumar, Assistant Director PG; Deans, staff and students participated in the program.

title: RUSA grant for St. Philomena’s college (Autonomous), Mysore
summary: RUSA grant for St. Philomena’s college (Autonomous), Mysore
content: RUSA grant for St. Philomena’s college (Autonomous), Mysore

Ministry of Human resource development (MHRD) has selected St. Philomena’s College, Mysore for the release of a grant amounting to Rs. 5 crores under Rashtriya Uchchatar Shiksha Abhiyan (RUSA) scheme under component 8 for achieving the desired target of ‘Academic excellence in Higher Education.’ A total of 17 colleges in India and 5 colleges in Karnataka have been selected under this scheme.

In a communication by the Karnataka State Higher Education Council (KSHE) through the Department of Collegiate Education and also on the website of MHRD (RUSA) under the ‘Minutes of Project Approval Board Meeting’ held on 25th May 2018, it is stated that the grant to be released by the MHRD to St.Philos is exclusively for ‘Enhancing Quality and Excellence in Select Autonomous Colleges’ under component 8 of RUSA scheme. Colleges with NAAC CGPA 3.51 and above under the UGC’s Autonomy Regulations 2018 will be supported to enhance quality of teaching and research under this grant.

This grant would provide new dimension in strengthening the infrastructure resources and would help in providing quality and branding in higher education. Further the grants will also be utilized for creation of new facilities, renovation and up gradation of existing facilities and for procuring new equipments both at the PG and UG level.

Construction of new classrooms, toilets, computer labs, renovation like modernization and strengthening of laboratories, sports facilities, academic and administrative blocks, hostels, strengthening of libraries and access to knowledge resource and procurement of furniture and fixtures will be the key areas for which the grant is to be utilised. An Institutional Development Plan (IDP), physical and financial outlay and proposed strategic plan (for 5-10 years) have to be prepared by the college in utilising the approved grant in time bound manner as well as following the norms of the MHRD and KSHE with an objective quality enhancement and excellence.

title: Professional Enrichment Program-Report
summary: Education helps to accelerating the speed among students; in education everything happens by design and nothing by default, said Prof. C.G Venkatesha Murthy, Dean Research, Regional institution of education, Mysore
content: Education helps to accelerating the speed among students; in education everything happens by design and nothing by default, said Prof. C.G Venkatesha Murthy, Dean Research, Regional institution of education, Mysore

In the workshop organized by St.Philomena’s college in collaboration with IQSC has organized two days workshop on Professional Enrichment Program for the faculties of the college on June 1 and June 2, 2018 at college auditorium.

He added, education is a process of man making where professional are governed by codes of ethics, integrity and morality. Emphasized on research and its importance in the teaching profession where teaching should become the byproduct of research.
Teaching is the profession which always scope for change and growth which helps the teachers in learning and also to provide quality education to their students, he added
Prof.Venkatesha also briefed the faculties on profession, professionalism, professional development on his key note address.

Profession that constantly evolving is teaching profession and as a teachers we should always be open for learning and growing, said Rev Fr Dr. Bernard Prakash Barnis, Rector/manager, St.Philomena’s college.

Rev Fr Dr. Bernard Prakash Barnis, Rector/manager, Rev.Fr.Maria Xavier , vice Rector, Dr.RuthShantha Kumari, principle, Prof.Sanjay Nair , Vice Principle, Rev Fr.Rony Ravikumar, assistant director PG, Prof.Ronald Prakash Kutina, IQSC Coordinator, all the Dean’s and HOD of all the departments and faculties were present in the workshop.
Time: 11.30 to 1.00 pm
Topic: Role of teachers in holistic development of Students (Brain Storming)
Resource Person: Prof. C.G.Venkatesh Murthy, Dean- Research, Regional Institute of Education, Mysore.
The teachers should first develop the vision, mission and goal of the Institution so that it would help in development of the college as well as the students.
As a teacher we should concentrate more on the learning, speaking, reading and writing skills of our students.

A teacher is not the one who just complete his / her subject but they should concentrate on the development of communication skills, leadership quality, personality development and skill development of the students.
It was a brain storming session where it was an open session for participants to put up their opinion on few questions which speaker asked like:

What are your explicitly doing to fulfil these goals? And he suggested teachers to take up this task if they are not practicing and to remember that not all children learn the same and each individual differ.

All together the participants gave 72 suggestions where he suggested the IQAC to put up all the suggestions and work on it, and explained how teachers can play an important role in the searching the high level through ZPD method and he stressed on telling teachers to be comfortable first then they can help the students to achieve their goal.
Session was for discussion and interaction, participants clarified their doubt.
Time: 2.00 to 3.30 pm
Resource person: Dr. Kumaswamy, Lecturer, CTE, Mangalore
In this session, speaker explained on vision aspects of teaching, learning and evaluation method.
He explained teaching is an act of giving/passing on information where learning is an act of receiving information.
To construct information in to knowledge the teaching should be an act of facilitating learning and learning will be an act of constructing knowledge.

He also briefed teachers that if their teaching does not develop their personality, attitude and unable to take decision then you have just merely passed information but to do this they don’t need a teacher and classroom they get information through internet so as a teachers we should more concentrate on how we are moulding our students for tomorrow.

As a teacher our learning process should be always continuous and we should restructure knowledge based on our experience. We should always Construct, De-Construct and Reconstruct our knowledge which helps us in continuous learning process.

Speakers asked participants many questions where he didn’t wanted them to answer it, he just wanted them to think and question themselves as a teacher what are we doing and are we doing what we are telling the students. He also requested them to never stop thinking and questioning yourselves that process helps us in growing.
Session was open for discussion and participants classified their doubts.
Time: 3.0 to 5.00 pm
Topic: Assessment process and possibilities in CBCS context in Higher Education Institutions.
Resource Person: Prof. Anand, Retd. Professor, RIE Mysore, NCERT.
Prof. Raveesha, Retd. Professor, UOM.
Prof. C.G.Vnkatesha Murthy, DEE & DEAN, Research, RIE, Mysore.
Panel Discussion on:

Basic aspiration of CBCS are – Continuous and comprehensive evaluation, flexibility for students to choose their paper and students centric curriculum. Challenges/anxiety for teachers to understand CBCS: It’s a credit based system and not marks based system teachers should understand dis first. When it comes to CBCS pattern of evaluation each semester has 16 weeks, 8 th week will be C1, 15 th week C2 and C3 is the final and end semester Exam. In CBCS the teachers who teaches is the best person to access the students. Guidelines for Inputs: whatever method you teach, fist teacher should be confident / aware of the topic and comfortable on the topic. As a teacher you should enjoy the topic when you don’t then you can’t expect better answer from the students.
Techers should concentrate on Average and below Average students and should have transparency and commitment.
When it comes to evaluation first discuss in the department then it should be known to students on what kind of evaluation method they got through.
Discussion was open for interaction and teachers classified their doubts.
Time: 8.30 to 10am
Topic: Stream/department group Discussion
Stream wise all the departments were divided into 3 groups Arts & Languages/ Science/ Commerce & Management.
All the groups came up with the roadmap for assessments and evaluation under departmental level and also for the professional development for the teachers.

Each group came up with their own ideas and innovative method of evaluation and discussed with each other and handed over their method list to the IQSC so that the management can take those methods for further development.
Time:10.00 to 11.30 am
Topic: Facilitating quality Assurance among college teachers.
Resource Person: Prof. C.G.Venkatesh Murthy, Dean, Research, RIE, Mysore

Prof. Venkatesh Murthy explained about what is quality where he told constantly pursuing excellence making sure that what your organization does it fit for the purpose and not only stay that way, but keeps on improving, helps in managing the quality.

He also explained on quality control which is a process by which entities review the quality of all factors involved in production which was continued by quality assurance which helps in preventing the mistakes or defect which assures quality for itself.
He also explained the principles of quality assurance principles that is, fit for purpose ans correct the mistakes in the first time.
He also mentioned on the challenges of quality assurance they are:
Presage factor Context factor Process factor Product factor In the session speaker explained about the IQSC and its function ad what are the professional responsibilities of an educational leader.
A teacher is a professional, educational leader, adviser, colleague, well-wisher and role model and a principal/teacher of a college can assure quality in his/her college.
The session was open for discussion.
Reflation and Valediction

Teaching profession is the profession which has major impact on the younger generation so faculty enrichment programs like this helps in the professional growth of the teachers and also acts like an instructor for all of us to know where we stand and which all the area’s that we need to improve for the professional growth said, Dr. Ruth Shantha Kumari, Principal in her valedictory remarks, feedback of all the session were taken by the participants.
Prof. Ronald Prakash Cutinuh, IQSC co-ordinator proposed Vote of Thanks.

Rev Fr Dr. Bernard Prakash Barnis, Rector/manager, Rev.Fr.Maria Xavier , vice Rector, Dr.RuthShantha Kumari, principle, Prof.Sanjay Nair , Vice Principle, Rev Fr.Rony Ravikumar, assistant director PG, Prof.Ronald Prakash Cutinuh, IQSC Coordinator, all the Dean’s and HOD of all the departments and faculties were present in the workshop.

content: St. Philomena’s College organizes the TEDx event of international fame St. Philomena’s College organized TEDx SPC, the independently organized TED event in the college auditorium on 29 th April 2018. The event was inaugurated by His Highness Yaduveer Krishnadatta Chamaraja Wadiyar, the Maharaja of Mysore. Dr Thomas Antony Vazhapilly, Bishop Emeritus presided over the event. Other Guests included Msgr.Rev. Leslie Moras, The Episcopal Vicar of MDES and Dr. T. Ruth Shantha Kumari, the principal of the college.

His Highness Yaduveer Krishnadatta Wadiyar Spoke about how important the event was in maintaining the rich heritage of Mysore city, wherein such meaningful discourses happen regularly. He referred to some instances from history where similar discussions were taking place in the courts of Mysore.

The event successfully took place in the college auditorium with a houseful audience of 100 people. 16 speakers who had expertise in different fields such as climate change, health and lifestyle, art and entertainment and interfaith harmony shared their ideas for sustained social development.

The Sponsors for the event were Task Education Charitable Welfare Trust, Bharath International tours and Travels, Forum Centre mall, Kornish Café, 21 degrees, Techref Solutions Pvt Ltd., and Honnasiri Nissan.
The event concluded with vote of thanks by the organizer and co-organizer thanking the audience and the speakers and saplings were distributed to all the attendees.

title: Graduation Day 2018
summary: Graduation Day 2018 was held at 10 am on Monday, 19 th March 2018 in the College Indoor Stadium.
content: Graduation Day 2018 was held at 10 am on Monday, 19 th March 2018 in the College Indoor Stadium.
The outgoing students of all UG streams (485) and PG Departments (199) participated in the program.
Dr (Fr) Eugine Lobo, Secretary, Karnataka Regional Commission for Education and PRO Karnataka Regional Catholic Bishops’ Council, Bangalore, delivered the Graduation Day address.
His Excellency Rt. Rev. Dr. K.A. William Bishop of Mysore presided over the program.
Msgr.Rev.Fr.Leslie Moras Episcopal Vicar administered the oath to the students.

Mrs. Kaprangi Elizabeth, Deputy Administrator and responsible for Education, Mr.Manuambi Mindan Sexton, Deputy Administrator and CEO District Development Authority, were the special guests from Papua New Guinea.
Rector, Rev. Dr. Bernad Prakash Barnis , Principal Dr. Ruth Shanthakumari
Rev.Dr.M.Vincent Principal of PU College, Deans of all the stream (UG&PG) were presents
Retired staff members, members of executive committee of the alumni association, well-wishers and invited guests were present.

In his graduation day address, Dr (Fr) Eugine Lobo emphasized on the importance of personal integrity in one's life and he advised the students to finish the tasks that they take up in life with commitment. Quoting Abraham Lincoln he said we are bound to be true not just to win and to live up to what light we have and not just to succeed. He urged the students to be grateful to the parents and teachers throughout their life. He advised the outgoing graduates to have Competence, Compassion and Commitment and to learn from their mistakes.
In his presidential address bishop of Mysore stressed on respecting each other to have a more meaningful life.

title: BVOC
summary: It has been a long felt necessity to align higher education with the emerging needs of the economy so as to ensure that the graduates of higher education system have adequate knowledge and skills for employment and entrepreneurship. The higher education system has to incorporate the requirements of various industries in its curriculum, in an innovative and flexible manner to produce holistic and well groomed graduates.
content: It has been a long felt necessity to align higher education with the emerging needs of the economy so as to ensure that the graduates of higher education system have adequate knowledge and skills for employment and entrepreneurship. The higher education system has to incorporate the requirements of various industries in its curriculum, in an innovative and flexible manner to produce holistic and well groomed graduates.

On these lines, the University Grants Commission (UGC) had launched a scheme on 27 February, 2014 for skills development based higher education as part of college/university education, leading to Bachelor of Vocation (B.Voc.) degree with multiple entry and exit points.

The B.Voc. programme enables the graduates completing B.Voc to make a meaningful participation in accelerating India’s economy by gaining appropriate employment, becoming entrepreneurs and creating appropriate knowledge base.
Objectives of B.Voc. programme

To provide judicious mix of skills and general education relating to the profession. To ensure that the students have adequate knowledge and skills, so that they are work ready at each exit point of the programme To provide flexibility to students by means of pre-defined entry and multiple exit points To enhance employability of the graduates and meet industry requirements Courses offered under B.Voc .:
B.Voc. in Media and Entertainment:

Desktop publishing Photography Creative advertising Script writing Technical writing Television production Film journalism Radio production Cinematography Media partners Internship Placement opportunities B.Voc. in Healthcare Technology :
Industry partners Internship and placement 100% job placement General Components
Apart from the main components the course also offers other subjects like
English Life skills Computer Application For enabling the candidate to be more efficient and constructive .
Entry and Exit Lateral entry The course also offers lateral entry option where graduate drop-outs can take admission into any academic year of the course.
Early exit Diploma, advanced diploma, Bachelors If a student discontinues the course :
After the completion of one year of the course, he shall receive a Diploma. After the completion of two years of the course, he shall receive an Advanced Diploma. Eligibility:
10+2 (PUC), Graduate drop-outs.
Rupees 10,000 will be charged as course fee for the programme.
Hostel facility for girls
Community College programme (One Year) UGC Approved.

Diploma in Medical Lab Technology Diploma in Healthcare The Course certificates will be awarded by the University of Mysore. We guarantee a 100% placement for the participants for the course. The course also offers a stipend for the students who are from poor economic background. Fee amount will be nominal.
Pass in PUC or 12 th standard in any stream.

content: The Placement Cell strives to achieve excellent placement of students each year. Placement Cell aims at developing the overall personality and competency of the students. The Placement Cell also undertakes many activities.
Activities / Highlights
Some highlights of the placement Cell:

Hard work, commitment and a rare sense of dedication to the profession that all our past recruiters come every year to recruit the students. Enhancing industry-academia Industrial Training, and Guidance under Corporate Action Plan. Assisting in improving the employability of the students by organising special training with the help of experts from industry. Organising campus recruitments. Arranging In-Plant training with leading companies. Establishing and maintaining effective corporate relations. Making available counseling and career development services to students. Improving the quality of placements in terms of job opportunities, companies of relevance that visit the campus and the highest and average salaries. Ensuring maximum visibility of the institution to the corporate world through frequent visits, interactions with the top management and Project Guidance under Corporate Action Plan. Obtaining feedback from employers on the performance of students to enhance the quality of students. Assisting in improving the employability of the students by organising special training with the help of experts from industry. List of Companies

Concentrix Sysinformation Pvt Ltd Infosys Wipro TCS MMODAL PeoplePro TechMahindra IGate HDFC Goan Institute of Communicative English (GICE) Nobel Institute of Communicative English (NICE) Thomson Reuters training
The placement Cell co-ordinated the Thomson Reuters training in Financial Markets

Thomson Reuters Corporation is a Multinational Mass-Media and Information Company. Thomson Reuters was ranked as Canada's "leading corporate brand" in the 2010 Inter-brand Best Canadian Brands ranking. Thomson Reuters operates in more than 100 countries, and has more than 60,000 employees around the world. TR works in various sectors such as Financial, Risk Management Solutions, Intellectual Property, Legal, Pharmacy & Life Sciences, Reuters News Agency, Tax & Accounting, Scholarly & Scientific Research.

Thomson Reuters as its CSR initiative along with GTT and NASSCOM foundation skilled the our 51 final year B.Com and BBM students for 100 hrs by corporate certified trainers and skill development partners for better career opportunities in financial markets and included personal-mentoring and grooming the trainee beneficiaries. The training bridged the gap between campus and corporate which was useful, informative and enhanced their knowledge in financial analysis.
